provenance.result_labels: MEASURED unless stated; clients are virtual (single machine)

he.arithmetic: approximate over reals (additions and multiplications, rescaling)
he.fit: best for real-valued updates; error ~1e-8 observed
exact but forces quantisation and a plaintext-modulus overflow bound

he.plaintext_domain: integers mod n (float via exponent encoding)
he.security_basis: decisional composite residuosity; broken by quantum (Shor)
he.fit: no SIMD: one ciphertext per coordinate -> impractical for NN updates

protocols.threat_model: honest-but-curious server (+ colluding clients below threshold t); dropout tolerant
protocols.limits: only linear aggregation; cannot run robust (median/Krum) rules; needs interaction rounds

protocols.computes: sums (and limited depth products) under encryption
protocols.threat_model: honest-but-curious server; secret-key holder must be trusted/not colluding with server
protocols.limits: ciphertext expansion, single secret key => key-holder is a single point of failure (no threshold HE here)

protocols.computes: arbitrary arithmetic circuits (here: sum, squared norm)
protocols.threat_model: dishonest majority among m servers (m-1 corrupted), MAC check detects active cheating (abort)
protocols.crypto: additive sharing + information-theoretic MAC + Beaver triples
protocols.limits: m servers must be non-colluding organisations; offline phase here = trusted dealer

decision.use: Primary HE scheme for real-valued model-update aggregation
decision.why: lowest ciphertext expansion and encryption cost among tested, approximate error far below SGD noise, no quantisation design needed
decision.rejected: BFV (exact but 1.3x larger ciphertext at tested params and needs fixed-point headroom); Paillier (no SIMD; ~2 orders of magnitude slower per element)

decision.why: no heavy public-key work per coordinate; tolerates dropout
decision.rejected: n/a (not exclusive with HE/SMPC; different threat model)

decision.use: Verified computation beyond sums (norm checks) / multi-institution compute servers
decision.why: supports multiplication (Beaver) so norm-bound checking is possible without revealing updates
